To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HAART initiated in neonates resulted in HIV eradication, but this was not sustained when HAART was discontinued.
HAART started in the first days after birth can result in HIV eradication, but this is not sufficient for long-term protection.
HAART initiated in early infancy resulted in HIV eradication in the short term, but that the virus could be reactivated upon discontinuation of treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the treatment of HIV infection and AIDS, and the development of a vaccine against HIV infection.
the development of a new generation of HIV drugs that will target and kill all HIV-infected cells.
the development and application of new technologies to the study of the human genome, and with the use of this knowledge to understand and treat disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAART initiated in infancy is able to control virus replication, to restore the immune system, and to prevent HIV-related disease, but not to eradicate the virus from the host.
HAART is not curative but is life-saving and life-prolonging.
the infant's HIV infection is not eradicated despite HAART, and that the virus is not eradicated by HAART.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV can be suppressed but not eradicated with current therapy.
HAART started in infancy can achieve HIV eradication in a minority of children but is not sufficient for HIV eradication in the majority.
HAART initiated in neonates, even in the absence of detectable viremia, does not lead to HIV eradication, as the virus persists in a latent reservoir and can be reactivated by HAART withdrawal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in a newborn who is treated with antiretrovials very early, HIV can be reactivated and cause disease.
, despite a complete and durable response to HAART, HIV infection is never cured.
HIV infection is not eradicated in infants treated with HAART, despite the absence of HIV replication and provirus in PBMC.
